mathematical_state.global_local_gain: Remains fully closed at its original v0.49 scope.
mathematical_state.scope: The full CutGivesAlt theorem has a human proof. The original Galois preconditions and four ties give a single good cut with all norm-choice facts and all four ties. The alternate family satisfies the simultaneous denominator estimate with its native hypotheses. Six Galois preconditions and the first and third of the four original compatibilities are produced on each supplied original member. Type-prime congruence lengths have exact Hecke restriction formulas. The point-dependent local cuts, cohomological bounds and weighted return to the uncut family retain the original integral arithmetic and the family quantifiers. The remaining selected-member hypotheses and the outstanding input for the uniform integral crystalline lifting estimate are described in the reading guide.

new_original_endpoints: P84B1 proves CutGivesAlt with the same cut and transported norm choice. P84C1 corrects LN1’s indexing of the central operator by coefficients of arbitrary monic polynomials. C84F4 and C84F5 give G5 and G6 on the cut.

M84T2 and M84T10 prove TieInePoly and tieChi on each supplied original member. M84T6 supplies large, nct, same, block and muUnr. L84C3 supplies c2. M84T7 and M84T9 give the localized section and the two inertia-polynomial laws on that member.

V84A5 proves ConclF and LinkN from the alternate family hypotheses with their own small-prime assertion. P84B2 restores the original family under the point estimates with the original finiteness and summability tests.

P84D2 identifies the point ideal length with a difference of two integral indices. P84D4–P84D5 construct the point-dependent type locus and show that its smaller ideal tests suffice with C equal to the local lifting constant.

T84L1–T84L6 give the conditional lifting and the direct and dual finite local quotient bounds. S84G1–S84G3 pass from local defects to the global cut ideal with a possibly nonunit root difference and all original class group and cyclotomic length contributions.
K84P1–K84P4 give the common type-prime potentially crystalline family. P84B3 reduces the bound on families with preconditions and four ties to uniform quantitative integral lifting.

Q84T1–Q84T5 give the interpolation denominator bound and the tame and coefficient reduction for the absolute constant 40, with the integral monodromy inputs explicit. F84R1–F84R3 prove the Frobenius estimate modulo powers of the prime and transfer sharp exponents to the invariant lattices.

denominator_family.hypotheses: On the original F78D2 family under Hypotheses₂, TwGood and FactsF with nonnegative family constant, choose C2 ≥ 122 before the common cutoff. The native ShaFinOdd guard asks for finite Galois cohomology lengths at every prime, including 2, for each integer 0 < e < t. The LinkN bound also retains summability of its cyclotomic vvTerm.
denominator_family.scope_of_bb: All guarded split and inert primes, including nonempty split columns on the selected twist. The original coarse constant is 120 and the resulting error constant is 7200.
denominator_family.scope_of_typ: Both original type primes and all lifts, with the paired-character field of the native FactsF assumption.
denominator_family.scope_of_large: CongBound_at holds for each sufficiently late member satisfying Facts on every localization passing its original large-prime guards and every admissible family, point and complement. The coefficient enlargement tests apply to the actual cut generators and descend. This gives Concl.large simultaneously with the preceding eleven fields.
denominator_family.scope_of_ram: For the original twisted indices at p=q,d and their good points, the integral rank estimate at 160 and the complete character estimate on the same local data yield the all-row inequality. The coefficient 2080 and nonnegative polynomial 181 f²t²(r+t) log b suffice. J78H2 gives Concl.ram with the same family constant as J80H2.

middle_range_progress.inert_global: A83G1 applies G82I1–G82I2 at each guarded inert C or D point. A83G2 combines this with B82R3 for the remaining inert row and G82C5 for split primes to obtain StarAD.

middle_range_progress.remaining: The residual Galois preconditions and compatibility data on the original selected members and the integral type-prime point bound on the chosen cut. See the current reading guide for the uniform crystalline-lifting input and the conditional cohomological route.
middle_range_progress.inert_rows_C_D: Every guarded inert C or D index, every good point and every tested map on the common hub. T83A6 supplies all-thick places, N82I1 all-nonthick places, and A83G1 assembles the signed mixed places.
middle_range_progress.inert_row_B: All guarded indices and good points with C2 >= 122, chosen before the common family cutoff (B82R3).
middle_range_progress.edition_83: The full middle-range estimate StarAD holds at every guarded split and inert index and every good point on the qualifying family. All fifteen Concl fields hold on the same hub, giving ConclF and LinkN with the original finiteness and summability hypotheses. A83G4 reduces GLOBAL_DENOMINATOR to a sufficient family-facts condition on the original class Des(C,3). The formal cut route requires its own arithmetic hypotheses and a comparison back to the uncut family. T83C3 transports the four compatibility conditions to every cut when they hold on the original datum. For counting, the definite row formula, rational near-term rigidity and arithmetic flag counts are proved. The indefinite trace still requires the stated analytic and measure estimates.
